les: Alles wat jy doen, kos energie
kaps_punt: Energie vir lewe: ons gebruik energie vir alles wat ons doen; ons kry energie uit voedsel; energie in ons voedsel kom van die Son (plante gebruik die energie van die Son om voedsel te maak vir hulself en vir diere en mense)

items.bewering: 'n Bal lê stil in die gras, en hy rol nie vanself weg nie. Iemand moet hom skop, of die wind moet hom stoot.
items.bron: A body at rest stays at rest unless a force acts on it (Newton's first law); kicking and wind both transfer energy to the ball. Britannica Kids, 'energy': https://kids.britannica.com/kids/article/energy/353100. Checked in full this round. The ball is specified as lying still in grass, so the slope case does not arise.

items.bewering: 'n Vuur brand ook nie sonder iets om te brand nie, soos hout of kole. Hoe langer die vuur brand, hoe minder hout bly daar oor.
items.bron: Fire triangle: fuel, heat and oxygen are all required, and a fire goes out once it has consumed its burnable fuel. US National Park Service, 'Wildland Fire Facts: There Must Be All Three': https://www.nps.gov/articles/wildlandfire-facts-fuel-heat-oxygen.htm; Wikipedia, 'Fire triangle'. The sentence names fuel only and does not claim fuel is the only requirement, so it is true as written.

items.bewering: Niks gebeur sonder dat iets anders iets weggee nie.
items.bron: The standard primary-level statement of energy transfer: a change happens when energy passes from one thing to another (Britannica Kids, 'energy': https://kids.britannica.com/kids/article/energy/353100; NSTA Science and Children, 'Q: What is energy?': https://www.nsta.org/science-and-children/science-and-children-septemberoctober-2021/q-what-energy). Limit noted, not a fault: a learner may think of a ball rolling down a slope or fruit falling 'vanself'. There the energy comes from the object's height, which is a Grade 4-level gap rather than a contradiction of the sentence.

items.bewering: Analogy across the first two blocks: a fire uses up its wood as it burns, and in the same way 'Jy gee ook iets weg wanneer jy stil op 'n stoel sit' (the body uses up food energy), which leads to 'Daarom raak jy weer honger'.
items.blok: Niks gebeur vanself nie / Ook wanneer jy stilsit
items.bron: Mapping checked. Cellular respiration, like burning, combines food (fuel) with oxygen to release energy, giving off carbon dioxide, water and heat (Britannica Kids, 'cellular respiration': https://kids.britannica.com/students/article/cellular-respiration/603291). Fuel used up means fuel must be replaced, which maps soundly onto needing to eat again. The lesson never says the body is on fire or that food burns inside you, so the comparison does not lead a learner toward flames or burning.

items.bewering: Jy gee ook iets weg wanneer jy stil op 'n stoel sit. ... Al hierdie stil werk kos jou energie.
items.bron: Basal metabolic rate: the energy the body uses at complete rest for breathing, circulation and cell growth and repair. Better Health Channel (Victoria Government), 'Metabolism': https://betterhealth.vic.gov.au/health/conditionsandtreatments/metabolism; Healthline, 'How to calculate your basal metabolic rate'.

items.bewering: Binne-in jou gaan party van die lewensprosesse dag en nag aan. Jou asemhaling hou aan.
items.bron: Breathing and cellular respiration continue during sleep, and resting metabolism includes breathing. Better Health Channel, 'Metabolism': https://betterhealth.vic.gov.au/health/conditionsandtreatments/metabolism. 'Party van' is correctly limited, since reproduction, for example, does not go on day and night.

items.bewering: Jou groei hou ook aan, en jou lyf bou en herstel homself sonder ophou.
items.bron: In children, growth hormone is released mostly during sleep, with smaller amounts during the day, and it drives growth and tissue repair. Frontiers in Endocrinology 2023 review: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/endocrinology/articles/10.3389/fendo.2023.1332114/pdf; NIEHS Factor, Nov 2022: https://www.niehs.nih.gov/news/factor/2022/11/papers/sleep-growth-hormone. Basal metabolism includes cell growth and repair at rest (Better Health Channel, above). 'Sonder ophou' is acceptable for continuous cell turnover. Growth itself comes in spurts, but the sentence says only that it continues, which holds for a child of this age.

items.bewering: 'n Skrapie op jou knie trek stadigaan weer toe.
items.bron: Minor scrapes heal over about 3 to 7 days as new skin forms from the edges and the wound shrinks. HealthLinkBC, 'How a Scrape Heals': https://www.healthlinkbc.ca/healthwise/how-scrape-heals; MedlinePlus: https://medlineplus.gov/ency/patientinstructions/000741.htm.

items.bewering: Uitskeiding gaan ook aan, en jou lyf raak heeltyd van sy afval ontslae.
items.bron: The lungs remove carbon dioxide, a waste of cellular respiration, with every breath, and the kidneys filter about 180 litres of blood a day to make urine. Thompson Rivers University Human Biology, 'Organs of Excretion': https://humanbiology.pressbooks.tru.ca/chapter/18-2-organs-of-excretion/. 'Heeltyd' holds because CO2 is exhaled continuously.

items.bewering: Energie is wat nodig is om iets te laat gebeur, beweeg of werk.
items.bron: The common primary-level definition: energy is the ability to do work and to make things move or happen. Britannica Kids, 'energy': https://kids.britannica.com/kids/article/energy/353100; NSTA, 'Q: What is energy?' (above). It simplifies 'capacity to do work' without becoming false.

items.bewering: Jy loop skool toe, en jy speel en hardloop op die sportveld. / Jy dra 'n swaar sak en help by die huis. / Jy praat met jou maats, en jy leer nuwe werk.
items.bron: Physical activity adds energy use above the basal rate (Better Health Channel, 'Metabolism', above). The brain uses about 20% of the body's energy, and effortful thinking and learning add a small extra amount. Live Science, 'How Many Calories Can the Brain Burn by Thinking?': https://livescience.com/burn-calories-brain.html. The list says these activities cost energy, not how much, so the small cost of learning makes it true.

items.bewering: 'n Voël vlieg oor die dak en bou sy nes. / 'n Mol grawe, en 'n eend swem oor die dam. / 'n Bok hardloop en soek kos in die veld.
items.bron: All of these are muscle work powered by cellular respiration (Britannica Kids, 'cellular respiration': https://kids.britannica.com/students/article/cellular-respiration/603291). Each behaviour is real for the animal named: in South Africa 'mol' covers golden moles and mole-rats, and both dig.

items.bewering: Iets moet jou dus ook energie gee, en dit is jou kos.
items.blok: Jou kos gee jou die energie
items.bron: Cellular respiration releases the chemical energy stored in food molecules. Britannica Kids, 'cellular respiration' (above); Berkeley Understanding Global Change, 'Respiration': https://ugc.berkeley.edu/background-content/respiration/.

items.bewering: Dink aan 'n oggend wanneer jy nog niks geëet het nie. Jy kan lam en sleg voel ... Ná 'n bord kos kan jy weer sterk genoeg voel om te speel.
items.blok: Jou kos gee jou die energie
items.bron: Fatigue, low energy and weakness are recognised signs of hunger, and they are relieved by eating. Boston Children's Hospital, 'Nutrition: why so hungry?': https://www.childrenshospital.org/programs/new-balance-foundation-obesity-prevention-center/problem-solvers/nutrition-why-so-hungry; Boston Children's Fitkit, 'Listen to what your body is telling you': https://fitkit.childrenshospital.org/node/24. The sentences are hedged with 'kan', which is correct: controlled evidence that skipping breakfast reliably causes tiredness is weak, so an unhedged version would overstate it.

items.bewering: Jy gebruik heeldag energie, en tog raak daardie energie nooit weg nie. Dit gaan net oor na iets anders.
items.bron: Conservation of energy and the first law of thermodynamics applied to the human body. Michigan State University Open Books, College Physics, 'Work, energy and power in humans': https://openbooks.lib.msu.edu/collegephysics1/chapter/work-energy-and-power-in-humans-2. The absolute 'nooit' is correct here.

items.bewering: Jou kos se energie gaan oor in alles wat jy doen en in warmte. Daardie warmte gaan uit jou lyf na alles om jou. Al daardie energie is nog daar, net nie meer binne-in jou nie.
items.bron: Food energy goes into work and heat, with by far the largest share becoming heat, which leaves the body. MSU College Physics, 'Work, energy and power in humans' (above). Limit noted, not a fault: surplus food energy is also stored as fat and in new tissue, and the lesson does not mention this. 'Al daardie energie' refers back to the energy that went into activity and heat, so as written it is true. A future revision should not widen it to say that ALL of a meal's energy leaves the body.

items.bewering: Daarom raak jy weer honger, en daarom moet jy weer eet.
items.bron: Hunger signals the need to replace energy used and low energy stores, as part of energy homeostasis. Boston Children's Fitkit, 'Listen to what your body is telling you': https://fitkit.childrenshospital.org/node/24; NCHPAD, 'Teaching kids to listen to their bodies': https://www.nchpad.org/resources/teaching-kids-to-listen-to-their-bodies-hunger-fullness-and-energy-signals/. The hormonal mechanism is simplified away, which is acceptable at this grade.

items.bewering: Die energie in jou kos was ook nie altyd in daardie kos nie. Jy weet al dat 'n groen plant sy eie kos met die son se lig in sy blare maak.
items.blok: Die son se energie sit in jou kos
items.bron: Photosynthesis takes place mainly in the leaves, where chloroplasts and chlorophyll capture light. University of Arizona Cooperative Extension, 'Basic Botany for Master Gardeners': https://extension.arizona.edu/sites/extension.arizona.edu/files/attachment/BasicBotanyforMaster%20Gardeners-2.pdf; UF/IFAS Extension, 'Plant Biology: Organs': https://blogs.ifas.ufl.edu/pascoco/?p=6321. 'Jy weet al' is an assumption about prior learning, not a claim about the world, and was not checked against the curriculum.

items.bewering: Die son se energie gaan so oor in die kos van die plant. Daar bly dit gebêre. Die plant kan dit self gebruik, of 'n dier of 'n mens kan die kos eet.
items.blok: Die son se energie sit in jou kos
items.bron: Light energy is stored as chemical energy in glucose and starch. The plant uses some of it in its own respiration and growth, and the energy held in plant tissue passes to the animal that eats it. Taylor & Francis ecology chapter: https://www.taylorfrancis.com/books/9781315640105/chapters/10.4324/9781315640105-8; Berkeley UGC, 'Respiration' (above).

items.bewering: Baie mense dink 'n plant kry sy kos uit die grond.
items.blok: Die grond gee geen kos nie
items.bron: Science-education research describes this misconception as 'universal and persistent' at all ages. Oak National Academy, 'Plant nutrition': https://www.thenational.academy/teachers/lessons/plant-nutrition; Cal Poly Pomona RESPECT, 'Common student ideas': https://www.cpp.edu/respect/resources/documents_5th/gr5.fw_common_student_ideas.pdf.

items.bewering: Die wortels suig wel water en 'n paar ander goed uit die grond op na die res van die plant. Maar nie een daarvan is kos nie, en die grond gee die plant geen kos nie.
items.blok: Die grond gee geen kos nie
items.bron: Roots take up water and mineral nutrients, which move up through the xylem. Sugars, the plant's food, come from photosynthesis, and water and minerals are not food. University of Arizona Cooperative Extension (above); Cal Poly Pomona RESPECT (above); Open University OpenLearn Create, 'Understanding plants': https://www.open.edu/openlearncreate/mod/oucontent/view.php?id=64820&section=9.2. 'Opsuig' reads as 'absorb' and is not a claim that the roots pump water up. The 'geen kos' absolute holds for green plants. Rare non-green plants that draw sugars from soil fungi lie well outside this lesson's frame.

items.bewering: 'n Plant maak sy eie kos, en hy gebruik dit eers self. 'n Bok kry daardie kos deur die plant se blare te vreet. Jy kry dit deur 'n appel of 'n bord pap te eet.
items.blok: Hoe die energie by jou uitkom
items.bron: Plants spend much of their captured energy on their own respiration and growth, and herbivores get what is held in the plant tissue (Taylor & Francis, above). Pap is cooked from white maize meal, a plant food. Pannar, 'The journey from white maize to pap': https://pannar.com/news-and-insights/the-journey-from-white-maize-to-pap.

items.bewering: Ons noem dit voeding, en dit is een van die sewe lewensprosesse.
items.blok: Hoe die energie by jou uitkom
items.bron: South African CAPS-aligned material lists seven life processes, with feeding (voeding) among them. CapeNature Grade 4 lesson plan: https://www.capenature.co.za/uploads/files/Lesson-Plan_Biodiversity_Living-and-non-living-structures-of-plants-and-animals_Grade-4_1hr.pdf; WCED ePortal Grade 4 lesson plan: https://www.wcedeportal.co.za/eresource/218791.

items.bewering: lewensprosesse: Die sewe dinge wat saam wys dat iets lewe.
items.bron: CapeNature and WCED Grade 4 lesson plans (above): the seven life processes are the features that together set living things apart from non-living things. 'Saam' is correctly chosen, since a single process taken alone does not mark something as alive.

items.bewering: voeding: Om kos te kry of kos te maak vir jou liggaam.
items.bron: Nutrition covers both obtaining food (animals) and making it (plants, by photosynthesis). Lumen Learning, 'Plant Nutrition': https://courses.lumenlearning.com/wm-nmbiology2/chapter/plant-nutrition/; Berkeley UGC, 'Respiration' (above).

items.bewering: asemhaling: Om energie uit jou kos te kry.
items.bron: As a life process, respiration is the release of energy from food in cells (MRS GREN 'Respiration'). Britannica Kids, 'cellular respiration' (above); Berkeley UGC, 'Respiration' (above). The Afrikaans word covers both breathing and respiration, and a Grade 8 Afrikaans natural-sciences lesson plan uses it for energy release from glucose (https://studylib.net/doc/27606476/lesplan-gr-8-natuurwetenskappe-k1-w1and2). Defining it as energy release, rather than as air in and out, also avoids the 'plants breathe with lungs' picture, so this is a scientifically sound choice.

items.bewering: Die meeste lewende dinge gebruik suurstof uit die lug of die water daarvoor.
items.bron: Berkeley Understanding Global Change, 'Respiration': https://ugc.berkeley.edu/background-content/respiration/: most organisms on land, in fresh water and in the oceans, plants included, use cellular respiration, while some bacteria use only anaerobic processes. Encyclopedia.com, 'aerobic': https://www.encyclopedia.com/science/encyclopedias-almanacs-transcripts-and-maps/aerobic-0: bacteria aside, most other living organisms need oxygen. 'Die meeste' is the correct quantifier. 'Alle' or 'byna elke' would be false because of anaerobic microbes, so the wording should not be tightened. Caveat: counted cell by cell, the share of Earth's microbes that live without oxygen is not established in the sources reached. This item rests on the encyclopedic consensus, not on a microbial census.

opsomming: Every claim was checked against outside sources and found true; there are no superlatives except 'die meeste' in the asemhaling entry, which is the correct quantifier and should not be tightened to 'alle' or 'byna elke', and the warning a writer most needs is not to widen 'Al daardie energie is nog daar, net nie meer binne-in jou nie' into a claim that all of a meal's energy leaves the body, because surplus is stored.
